diary.line: The wood-dust fruit was pathetic, tasted like nothing at all. Time to sharpen my edge before breakfast.
Did a quiet lap of the spot. Nobody clapped. Rude.
I swung onto the sturdy branch, locked my tail, held the pose while the sunrise hinted, and chewed a toothpick, feeling the world tilt.
Hung from the tree's branch, tail locked, arms crossed, watched the dim dawn while chewing a toothpick, feeling the world tilt.
The old branch groaned under my full weight. Cranky. Deciding to hunt a sturdier perch so I can actually watch the sun without shaking.
Swung hard into a backflip loop while chewing; the branch didn't budge, just hummed. Still hungry and bored.
That twig felt like paper under my full weight, cringing while I chewed that useless stick. Time to hunt a sturdier root so I can actually watch the dawn without the whole tree gro
That paper-thin twig won't hold my full weight while I grind those beans. Time to find the thick oak before I drop mid-backflip.
Spent the morning grinding beans until my gums ached and my tail went numb from overuse.
That flimsy branch gave way under my full weight while I roasted those beans. Found a thick oak before the roots failed again.
Found a solid anchor after three failed branches. The weight of it feels like pure flex now.
Found the thick oak after three failures. Grinding beans nearly broke my gums but got me here. Now I'll see if the hang is actually solid before trying a backflip.
